target_name: Serial dilution against a three-channel liquidity deficit
rationale: This is a cosmetic extension of the archive's gen-2 "Serial dilution with chronic cash shortfall" (identical financing leg, one extra moderator channel), and the stated justification is internally inconsistent because nesting SUMRANK weights cash-to-current-liabilities at 50% while the other two channels get 25% each rather than the claimed uniform weighting.

Cumulating gross repayments over three years is a defensible, pre-motivated temporal fix to the single-year version's zero FMB slope and shifts the construct from lumpy maturity timing to a persistent amortization burden, though gross dltr remains partly a mechanical proxy for debt-stock scale and the change from the archive signal is modest.

target_name: Industry-neutral serial dilution under cash shortfall
rationale: This merely stacks two already-tested archive modifications (IND_RANK of issuance; three-year cumulation) onto the same mechanism and moderator, which is a cosmetic recombination rather than a substantively different economic idea.

The expression matches the hypothesis (prior-payer screen, cut-positive sign, non-negative liquidity weight), the avoided-dilution mechanism is a genuinely new long-side channel rather than a sign-flipped rerun, and it is consistent with the gen-0 payout-revision slope, though the payer screen will likely compress coverage and the direction runs against the dividend-cut announcement literature so it needs to survive that tension.

target_name: Dilution scaled by liquid asset base
rationale: A single scaled-issuance ratio with no cross-theme interaction is close to a rediscovery of the well-known equity/net-external-financing issuance anomaly, and the current-assets denominator introduces small-denominator instability that winsorization only partly masks.

target_name: Gross capital-market turnover under liquidity stress
rationale: Testing gross financing turnover as a common factor behind the opposing issuance and repayment results is a legitimately discriminating experiment with a clear falsification, but the sum will be dominated by debt gross flows and thus risks becoming a leverage/debt-scale proxy rather than a clean dependence measure.
